```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(

))
release[catalog, on = "pg_id", `:=`(

)]

)

  theme_minimal(base_size = 10.5) +

      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

      plot.caption.position = "plot"
    )
)

comma <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
pct <- function(x, digits = 1) paste0(round(100 * x, digits), "%")
supp_table <- function(x, caption = NULL, widths = NULL, align = NULL, ...) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    preprint_kable(x, caption = caption, widths = widths, align = align, ...)
  } else {
    knitr::kable(x, caption = caption, align = align, ...)
  }
}
```

# Scope and reproducibility

This supplement documents the frozen Gutenberg Atlas release and provides a
worked demonstration of its use as a text corpus. The canonical release has
one row per Project Gutenberg book and is generated uniformly by the build
pipeline. Manual validation evaluates that pipeline; it does not patch
individual production rows.

All descriptive tables below are calculated from the frozen release files.
The reuse demonstration is rendered from held-out predictions and bootstrap
results generated by `02-models.Rmd`. Re-running that source report downloads
the sampled public-domain texts, reconstructs the text views, fits the models,
and overwrites the generated result files. Rendering this supplement itself
does not download texts or refit models.

The counts characterize books selected from Project Gutenberg. They are not
estimates of the historical population of English-language books or authors.

# Corpus construction

An eligible record is an English-language Project Gutenberg text with one
named personal author. Publication year is estimated from the earliest
HathiTrust record matched on normalized author surname and title. A record is
released only if its Project Gutenberg agent identifier resolves to a
Wikidata entity explicitly recorded as human and the matched year passes the
lifespan screen: at least 15 years after birth and no more than five years
after death. When death is unavailable, birth plus 90 years supplies the
upper bound. The release excludes matched years before 1700; later years are
retained and their lower validation accuracy is reported.

```{r funnel-table}
funnel[, decision := factor(decision, levels = decision)]
supp_table(
  funnel,
  col.names = c("Decision", "Books"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Corpus-construction funnel."
)
```

```{r funnel-figure, fig.cap="Corpus-construction funnel."}
funnel[, decision_plot := factor(decision, levels = rev(levels(decision)))]
ggplot(funnel, aes(decision_plot, N)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, fill = "grey35") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Books")
```

The pipeline releases `r comma(nrow(release))` of
`r comma(sum(funnel$N))` eligible records. The two largest exclusions are an
unmatched HathiTrust record and the absence of a deterministic Wikidata-human
link.

Exclusion is uneven by author era. Release rates vary much less by broad genre
or by Wikidata gender.

```{r release-rates}
candidates <- fread(file.path(data_dir, "unverified_candidates.csv"))
eligible <- rbind(
  release[, .(pg_id, birth, gender, released = TRUE)],
  candidates[, .(pg_id, birth, gender, released = FALSE)]
)
eligible[catalog, on = "pg_id", `:=`(
  subjects = i.subjects, locc = i.locc, bookshelves = i.bookshelves
)]
for (col in c("subjects", "locc", "bookshelves")) {
  set(eligible, which(is.na(eligible[[col]])), col, "")
}
eligible[, genre := assign_genre(bookshelves, subjects, locc)]
eligible[, birth_period := fcase(
  is.na(birth), "Unknown",
  birth < 1750, "Before 1750",
  birth < 1800, "1750-1799",
  birth < 1850, "1800-1849",
  birth < 1900, "1850-1899",
  default = "1900 or later"
)]
rate_rows <- function(d, by, label) {
  out <- d[, .(Eligible = .N, Released = sum(released)), by = by]
  setnames(out, by, "Group")
  out[, `:=`(Variable = label, `Release rate` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * Released / Eligible))]
  out[, .(Variable, Group, Eligible, Released, `Release rate`)]
}
birth_levels <- c("Before 1750", "1750-1799", "1800-1849", "1850-1899", "1900 or later", "Unknown")
by_birth <- rate_rows(eligible, "birth_period", "Author birth")
by_birth <- by_birth[order(match(Group, birth_levels))]
by_genre <- rate_rows(eligible[genre != "excluded"], "genre", "Broad genre")[order(-Eligible)]
by_genre[, Group := tools::toTitleCase(Group)]
by_gender <- rate_rows(eligible[gender %in% c("male", "female")], "gender", "Wikidata gender")[order(-Eligible)]
by_gender[, Group := tools::toTitleCase(Group)]
supp_table(
  rbind(by_birth, by_genre, by_gender),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Release rates among eligible books. Gender rows include only books whose author has a Wikidata gender claim.",
  label = "release-rates"
)
```

# Release composition

## Dates and match quality

`ht_year` is the earliest year among accepted HathiTrust candidates. It is an
estimate of first publication, not a claim that the selected holding is a
first edition. Matched years run from 1700 to 2004.

```{r dates-figure, fig.cap="Distribution of matched publication years."}
ggplot(release, aes(ht_year)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, boundary = 1700, fill = "grey35", color = "white") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "HathiTrust matched year", y = "Books")
```

```{r match-tier-table}
tier_counts <- release[, .N, tier][order(tier)]
tier_counts[, Definition := fifelse(
  tier == 1,
  "Exact normalized title within author surname",
  "Normalized-title prefix containment within author surname"
)]
supp_table(
  tier_counts,
  col.names = c("Match tier", "Books", "Definition"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "HathiTrust match tiers.",
  label = "match-tiers"
)
```

## Author metadata and linkage audit

Gender and country of citizenship are raw Wikidata P21 and P27 labels from
the dated snapshot. They are structured claims, not inferred attributes.
Coverage is measurable, but the values have not been independently validated
against a second biographical authority. Project Gutenberg and Wikidata
lifespan fields are retained separately; disagreements remain visible rather
than being silently resolved.

Raw citizenship labels name historical states, such as the Kingdom of Great
Britain or the Russian Empire, and often list the same country under several
names. `citizenship_modern` maps each of the 174 recorded labels to a
present-day state using `build/country_map.csv`, which assigns each historical
state to the successor that holds its core territory. Twenty-seven labels
involve a judgment call and are flagged in that file. The largest is the
Russian Empire (83 released books), which includes authors from present-day
Poland, Lithuania, Ukraine, and Finland.

```{r citizenship-modern}
modern <- release[citizenship_modern != "", .(
  country = trimws(unlist(strsplit(citizenship_modern, ";", fixed = TRUE)))
), by = pg_id]
top_modern <- modern[, .(Books = .N), .(`Present-day state` = country)][order(-Books)][1:10]
supp_table(
  top_modern,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Most frequent present-day states. Books with several states count once for each.",
  label = "citizenship-modern"
)
```

```{r author-audit}
coverage <- author_summary[grepl("coverage$", metric), .(
  Unit = tools::toTitleCase(unit),
  Field = sub(" coverage$", "", metric),
  Available = numerator,
  Total = denominator,
  Coverage = paste0(percent, "%")
)]
supp_table(
  coverage,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Wikidata field coverage.",
  label = "author-coverage"
)

agreement <- author_summary[grepl("agreement$", metric), .(
  Diagnostic = metric,
  Agree = numerator,
  Compared = denominator,
  Percent = paste0(percent, "%"),
  Note = note
)]
supp_table(
  agreement,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Cross-source linkage and lifespan diagnostics.",
  label = "author-agreement"
)
```

The release contains `r comma(uniqueN(release$agent))` resolved Project
Gutenberg agents. Surname-token agreement is a linkage diagnostic, and
lifespan agreement is cross-source corroboration; neither is an independent
accuracy estimate for Wikidata.

```{r author-composition}
per_author <- release[, .N, agent]
concentration <- data.table(
  Statistic = c(
    "Median books per author", "Mean books per author",
    "Authors represented by one book", "Books from the 100 most frequent authors"
  ),
  Value = c(
    comma(median(per_author$N)), sprintf("%.1f", mean(per_author$N)),
    comma(per_author[N == 1, .N]),
    comma(release[agent %in% per_author[order(-N)][1:100, agent], .N])
  )
)
supp_table(
  concentration,
  caption = "Author concentration.",
  label = "author-concentration"
)

top_authors <- release[, .(
  Books = .N,
  `Median age` = as.integer(median(ht_year - fcoalesce(birth, wd_birth), na.rm = TRUE)),
  `Middle range` = paste(quantile(ht_year - fcoalesce(birth, wd_birth), c(0.25, 0.75), type = 1, na.rm = TRUE), collapse = "--")
), .(Author = wd_label, Country = citizenship_modern, agent)][order(-Books)][1:10]
supp_table(
  top_authors[, .(Author, Country, Books, `Median age`, `Middle range`)],
  caption = "Ten most frequent authors in the release. Age at publication is matched publication year minus birth year; the middle range spans the 25th to 75th percentiles.",
  label = "top-authors"
)

gender_counts <- release[, .N, .(
  gender = fifelse(is.na(gender) | gender == "", "missing", gender)
)][order(-N)]
gender_counts[, Percent := pct(N / sum(N))]
supp_table(
  gender_counts,
  col.names = c("Raw Wikidata gender claim", "Books", "Percent"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Gender claims at book level.",
  label = "gender-composition"
)

top_citizenship <- release[
  !is.na(country_of_citizenship) & country_of_citizenship != "" &
    !grepl(";", country_of_citizenship),
  .N,
  country_of_citizenship
][order(-N)][1:8, country_of_citizenship]
release[, citizenship_group := fcase(
  is.na(country_of_citizenship) | country_of_citizenship == "", "Missing",
  grepl(";", country_of_citizenship), "Multiple claims",
  country_of_citizenship %in% top_citizenship, country_of_citizenship,
  default = "Other single claim"
)]
citizenship_counts <- release[, .N, citizenship_group][order(-N)]
citizenship_counts[, Percent := pct(N / sum(N))]
supp_table(
  citizenship_counts,
  col.names = c("Citizenship group", "Books", "Percent"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Country-of-citizenship claims at book level.",
  label = "citizenship-composition"
)
```

Historical country labels and multiple P27 claims are preserved. Thus, for
example, the United Kingdom and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and
Ireland remain distinct rather than being collapsed into a modern nationality.

## Deterministic broad genre labels

The canonical release does not add a single genre field. For description and
the reuse demonstration, Project Gutenberg bookshelves, subjects, and Library
of Congress classes supply four mutually exclusive analysis labels. Fiction,
poetry, and drama require one unambiguous creative-form signal. Nonfiction
requires no creative-form signal and a primary LoC class outside literature.
Conflicting or incomplete cases remain `excluded`.

```{r genre-table}
genre_counts <- release[, .N, genre][order(-N)]
genre_counts[, Percent := pct(N / sum(N))]
supp_table(
  genre_counts,
  col.names = c("Analysis label", "Books", "Percent"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Deterministic broad genre labels."
)
```

```{r genre-figure, fig.cap="Distribution of deterministic broad genre labels."}
ggplot(genre_counts, aes(reorder(genre, N), N)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, fill = "grey35") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Books")
```

# Publication-year validation

The validation sample contains 200 release books, stratified by matched period
and match tier, with at least eight sampled books per cell and the
remaining positions allocated in proportion to cell size (largest-remainder
rounding). Within each cell, books were drawn at random without replacement
using seed 20261021 (`build/15-validation-sample.R`). Author gender was not a
stratifying variable. Each resolved row has a cited reference year. A match is accurate when
the HathiTrust estimate is within one year of that cited year. One composite
Kipling edition remains ambiguous and receives no verdict.

The 16 sampled books dated 1925 or later had lower accuracy than the earlier
periods, most often because the earliest HathiTrust holding was a later
reprint. They remain part of the release and the weighted estimate.

The overall estimate combines within-stratum sample proportions using each
period-by-tier cell's share of the release. The early and late periods were
deliberately oversampled, so the weighted estimate—not the raw proportion—is
the headline result.

```{r validation-summary}
release[, validation_period := as.character(cut(
  ht_year, c(1699, 1799, 1849, 1899, 1924, 2100),
  labels = c("1700-99", "1800-49", "1850-99", "1900-24", "1925+")
))]
release_cells <- release[, .(`Books represented` = .N),
                         .(Period = validation_period, `Match tier` = tier)]
sample_design <- checked_all[, .(
  `Sampled books` = .N,
  `Judged books` = sum(!is.na(year_ok))
), .(Period = period, `Match tier` = tier)]
sample_design <- merge(sample_design, release_cells,
                       by = c("Period", "Match tier"))
supp_table(
  sample_design,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Stratified validation allocation and represented release counts.",
  label = "validation-design"
)

overall <- date_summary[scope == "overall_weighted" & group == "all", .(
  Judged = judged,
  `Accuracy within one year` = paste0(accuracy_percent, "%"),
  `95% interval` = paste0(ci_low_percent, "% to ", ci_high_percent, "%")
)]
supp_table(
  overall,
  caption = "Weighted publication-year accuracy.",
  label = "validation-overall"
)

period_accuracy <- date_summary[scope == "period_unweighted", .(
  Period = group,
  Judged = judged,
  Accuracy = paste0(accuracy_percent, "%")
)]
supp_table(
  period_accuracy,
  caption = "Accuracy by validation period.",
  label = "validation-period"
)

checked[, year_ok := as.logical(year_ok)]
judged <- checked_all[!is.na(true_year)]
judged[, absolute_gap := abs(ht_year - true_year)]
gap_table <- judged[, .(
  Books = .N,
  `Within one year` = pct(mean(absolute_gap <= 1)),
  `Within five years` = pct(mean(absolute_gap <= 5)),
  `Median absolute gap` = as.double(median(absolute_gap))
), period]
supp_table(
  gap_table,
  caption = "Absolute error by validation period.",
  label = "validation-gap"
)
```

## Validation sources

Sources for the validation years were chosen book by book, without a fixed
source hierarchy. Each cited source was classified after the fact by type
(`build/20-validation-evidence.R`). Catalogue records and digitized editions
date a particular edition. They establish first publication only when the
source note records first-edition evidence. Reference works,
contemporary reviews, general web pages, and trade listings assert first
publication directly. HathiTrust catalogue records, the same catalogue used
for matching, are cited for
`r sum(grepl("hathitrust", checked[!is.na(year_ok), year_source]))` dates.

```{r validation-evidence}
evidence_class <- fread(file.path(data_dir, "validation_evidence_by_class.csv"))
class_labels <- c(
  catalogue = "Catalogue record", general_web = "General web",
  edition = "Digitized edition", trade = "Trade listing",
  reference = "Reference or bibliography", contemporary = "Contemporary review or serial"
)
supp_table(
  evidence_class[, .(
    `Evidence class` = unname(class_labels[evidence_class]),
    Judged = judged,
    `Asserts first publication` = first_claim,
    `Accuracy (unweighted)` = paste0(accuracy_percent, "%")
  )],
  caption = "Validation years by evidence class.",
  label = "validation-evidence"
)

evidence_sens <- fread(file.path(data_dir, "validation_evidence_sensitivity.csv"))
supp_table(
  evidence_sens[, .(
    Subset = subset,
    Judged = judged,
    Cells = cells,
    `Weighted accuracy` = paste0(accuracy_percent, "%"),
    `95% interval` = paste0(ci_low_percent, "% to ", ci_high_percent, "%")
  )],
  caption = "Weighted accuracy under source restrictions. Estimates with fewer than eight cells are reweighted over the represented cells.",
  label = "validation-sensitivity"
)
```

No source restriction moves the weighted estimate by more than
`r sprintf("%.1f", max(abs(evidence_sens$accuracy_percent - evidence_sens$accuracy_percent[1])))` points.
The reported accuracy therefore does not depend on the weaker source types.

## Error taxonomy

The `r checked[as.logical(year_ok) == FALSE, .N]` errors consist of later-edition or reprint dates that pass the lifespan
screen, multi-volume records for which the HathiTrust year refers to the
set rather than the component represented by Project Gutenberg, and one
wrong-book match. The categories diagnose failure modes; they are not used to
manually correct the release.

```{r error-taxonomy}
multi_volume_ids <- c(19214L, 14464L, 76102L)
wrong_book_ids <- 56418L
errors <- checked[year_ok == FALSE]
errors[, error_type := fcase(
  pg_id %in% multi_volume_ids, "Multi-volume component/set mismatch",
  pg_id %in% wrong_book_ids, "Wrong-book match",
  default = "Later edition or reprint"
)]
error_counts <- errors[, .N, error_type][order(-N)]
supp_table(
  error_counts,
  col.names = c("Failure mode", "Books"),
  caption = "Taxonomy of publication-year errors."
)
```

Later editions and reprints are the dominant failure mode, including most
errors among matched years after 1924.

These errors have two consequences for analyses based on author lifespans.
First, they are asymmetric. In the validation sample,
`r errors[ht_year > true_year, .N]` of the `r nrow(errors)` errors place a
book later than its first publication, so ages at publication skew older and
an author's latest dates are the least reliable. Second, the lifespan screen
truncates ages by construction: no released book is dated before its author's
fifteenth birthday or more than five years after death. Age distributions near
either bound therefore reflect the release rule, not publishing history.
Author-level summaries should use medians or percentiles rather than minimum
and maximum ages, as in the author table above. A future improvement should be a general,
pre-specified rule evaluated on a new targeted sample, not a ledger of manual
corrections.

# Reuse demonstration: signal in book text

This demonstration asks whether a passage from each book carries information
recorded in the metadata. It is evidence that the release can support corpus
research, not an additional validation of individual metadata values.

Three held-out tasks predict broad genre, 25-year period, and publication
year. The date tasks use 1800--1924 as a fixed analytical window; this is not
a release boundary. Five-fold evaluation is author-disjoint, so all books by
an author remain in the same fold.

```{r model-sample}
demo_tasks <- c("genre", "period", "year")
sample_counts <- model_sample[task %in% demo_tasks, .(
  Books = .N,
  Authors = uniqueN(agent)
), .(Task = task, Class = class)]
supp_table(
  sample_counts,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Reuse-demonstration samples."
)
```

Each book contributes up to 5,000 words from its body after the Gutenberg
header and the first 400 post-marker words. Word and character TF–IDF models
use penalized regression; averaged BGE embeddings use ridge regression. Raw
opening-text models act as a front-matter check. Classification is evaluated
with macro-F1 and balanced accuracy; numeric year prediction uses mean
absolute error and correlation. Intervals come from 1,000 author-cluster
bootstrap samples.

```{r model-results}
model_names <- c(
  baseline = "Baseline", raw_word = "Raw opening, words",
  raw_char = "Raw opening, characters", body_word = "Body, words",
  body_char = "Body, characters", body_bge = "Body, BGE"
)

best_body <- rbindlist(lapply(demo_tasks, function(task_name) {
  candidates <- model_metrics[task == task_name & model %in% c("body_word", "body_char", "body_bge")]
  if (task_name == "year") candidates[which.min(mae)] else candidates[which.max(macro_f1)]
}))
baseline <- model_metrics[model == "baseline" & task %in% demo_tasks]
overview <- merge(baseline, best_body, by = "task", suffixes = c("_baseline", "_body"))
overview[, `:=`(
  Task = tools::toTitleCase(task),
  `Best body model` = unname(model_names[model_body]),
  Baseline = fifelse(task == "year", sprintf("%.1f years MAE", mae_baseline), sprintf("%.3f macro-F1", macro_f1_baseline)),
  `Body score` = fifelse(task == "year", sprintf("%.1f years MAE", mae_body), sprintf("%.3f macro-F1", macro_f1_body))
)]
supp_table(
  overview[, .(Task, `Best body model`, Baseline, `Body score`)],
  caption = "Best body-text result for each task."
)
```

Genre is strongly recoverable from body text. Period and continuous year also
show signal, though raw front matter improves temporal prediction.

## Complete model results

```{r complete-model-results, results="asis"}
fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, digits) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f [%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"), est, lo, hi)
}

for (task_name in demo_tasks) {
  digits <- if (task_name == "year") 1 else 3
  score_name <- if (task_name == "year") "Mean absolute error [95% CI]" else "Macro-F1 [95% CI]"
  score_quantity <- c("baseline", "raw_word", "raw_char", "body_word", "body_char", "body_bge")
  rows <- rbindlist(lapply(score_quantity, function(model_name) {
    b <- model_boot[task == task_name & quantity == model_name]
    g <- model_boot[task == task_name & quantity == paste0("gain_", model_name)]
    m <- model_metrics[task == task_name & model == model_name]
    data.table(
      Model = unname(model_names[model_name]),
      Score = fmt_ci(b$estimate, b$lo, b$hi, digits),
      Gain = if (nrow(g)) fmt_ci(g$estimate, g$lo, g$hi, digits) else "",
      Secondary = if (task_name == "year") sprintf("%.2f", m$r) else sprintf("%.3f", m$balanced_accuracy)
    )
  }))
  names(rows)[names(rows) == "Score"] <- score_name
  names(rows)[names(rows) == "Secondary"] <- if (task_name == "year") "Correlation" else "Balanced accuracy"
  cat("\n\n### ", tools::toTitleCase(task_name), "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(supp_table(
    rows,
    caption = paste("Complete held-out results:", task_name),
    label = paste0("model-results-", task_name)
  ))
}
```

## Confusion matrices {.tabset}

```{r confusion, results="asis"}
if (isTRUE(params$include_confusion_matrices)) {
  period_levels <- sprintf("%d-%d", seq(1800, 1900, 25), seq(1824, 1924, 25))
  for (task_name in demo_tasks) {
    pred <- copy(predictions[[task_name]])
    cat("\n\n### ", tools::toTitleCase(task_name), "\n\n", sep = "")
    for (model_name in c("body_word", "body_char", "body_bge")) {
      actual <- pred$class
      predicted <- pred[[model_name]]
      if (task_name == "year") {
        actual <- factor(pred$class, levels = period_levels)
        clipped <- pmin(pmax(predicted, 1800), 1924)
        predicted <- factor(assign_period25(round(clipped)), levels = period_levels)
      } else {
        lev <- sort(unique(actual))
        actual <- factor(actual, levels = lev)
        predicted <- factor(predicted, levels = lev)
      }
      tab <- as.data.table(table(Actual = actual, Predicted = predicted))
      wide <- dcast(tab, Actual ~ Predicted, value.var = "N", fill = 0)
      counts <- as.matrix(wide[, -1])
      wide[, Recall := round(diag(counts) / rowSums(counts), 2)]
      cat("\n\n#### ", model_names[[model_name]], "\n\n", sep = "")
      print(supp_table(wide))
    }
  }
} else {
  cat("Confusion matrices were omitted by the render parameter.")
}
```

# Limitations

The archive is shaped by public-domain law, volunteer selection, cataloguing,
and survival; it is not a representative sample of historical publishing.
HathiTrust dates sometimes identify a reprint or set rather than first book
publication. Wikidata demographic fields are dated public claims with uneven
coverage, especially for citizenship, and they should not be treated as
independently verified personal attributes. Broad genre labels are analysis
conveniences derived deterministically from catalog metadata. Finally, the
reuse models show association in this selected corpus and do not identify
essential properties of genres, periods, or author identities.
